# frozen_string_literal: true

# Reference implementation of a vendor mock transport, wired into nothing:
# no client selects it and no flag reaches it.
#
# Puts {TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::Instead::Mock::Router} where the socket
# would be.
#
# It sits at the bottom of the stack rather than in place of the client, so a
# request answered here still passes through the status-to-error mapping, the
# JSON parsing, the token ceremony and the metrics that a live request passes
# through. A stand-in above the middleware would demonstrate none of them.
#
# @api private
class TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::Instead::Mock::Adapter < Faraday::Adapter
  # @param env [Faraday::Env] the outgoing request
  # @return [Faraday::Response]
  def call(env)
    super

    status, headers, body = TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::Instead::Mock::Router.call(env, firm_id: firm_id)
    save_response(env, status, body, headers)

    @app.call(env)
  end

  private

  # Handed in when the connection is built, because the adapter has no access to
  # the connection row and the handles it mints are the firm's.
  #
  # @return [Integer]
  def firm_id
    @connection_options.fetch(:firm_id)
  end
end

class TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::BaseClient
  # @param vendor_connection [TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::HasOauthConnection]
  #   vendor connection row — the concern carries both halves the client needs: the
  #   token readers {TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::TokenRefreshable} drives and the
  #   state machine that records the grant's lifecycle. Named in full because the
  #   renewal runs beside `ActiveRecord::Base.connection`, which is a different
  #   thing entirely.
  # @param transport [Faraday::Adapter::Test::Stubs, nil] injected in specs; the
  #   default adapter is used in every other environment.
def initialize(vendor_connection, transport: nil)
    @vendor_connection = vendor_connection
    @transport = transport
  end

class TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::BaseClient
  # Which transport answers: the stub a spec injected, otherwise the process
  # default.
  #
  # @return [Array] arguments for `Faraday::RackBuilder#adapter`
def adapter_spec
    return [:test, transport] if transport

    [Faraday.default_adapter]
  end

require 'spec_helper'

RSpec.describe TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::BaseClient, :unit do
  include TaxAutomationsHelpers

  # A real subclass rather than a double: the base class IS a template method, so
  # the only honest way to exercise it is to fill its hooks. `ping` stands in for
  # any vendor call — every one of them goes through `request`.
  let(:client_class) do
    Class.new(described_class) do
      def self.name
        'TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::Testing::Client'
      end

      def ping
        request(:get, '/ping')
      end

      # A vendor whose answer is worth more than its parsed body maps it where
      # the request is made. The block sees the whole response.
      def ping_status
        request(:get, '/ping') { |response| [response.status, response.body['Status']] }
      end

      private

      def base_url
        'https://vendor.test'
      end

      def auth_headers(access_token)
        {'Authorization' => "Bearer #{access_token}"}
      end

      def refresh_tokens!
        {access_token: 'refreshed-access', refresh_token: 'refreshed-refresh', expires_in: 1.hour.to_i, refresh_expires_in: 30.days.to_i}
      end

      def vendor_error_message(body)
        return unless body.is_a?(Hash)

        body['Error']
      end

      def vendor_error_class(body)
        return unless body.is_a?(Hash)

        {'NO_SCOPE' => TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::BaseClient::InsufficientScopeError}[body['Reason']]
      end
    end
  end

  let(:firm) { create(:firm) }
  # The `:connected` trait leaves both tokens live, and the ceremony reads their
  # expiries on every request — an unexpired grant is the baseline here, not the
  # exception.
  let(:connection) { create(:instead_connection, :connected, firm:) }
  let(:client) { client_class.new(connection, transport: transport) }
  let(:transport) { Faraday::Adapter::Test::Stubs.new }

  context 'without vendor hooks' do
    let(:bare_class) do
      Class.new(described_class) do
        def self.name
          'Bare'
        end
      end
    end
    let(:bare) { bare_class.new(connection, transport: transport) }

    it 'raises NotImplementedError for #base_url until a vendor supplies it' do
      expect { bare.send(:base_url) }.to raise_error(NotImplementedError, /base_url/)
    end

    it 'raises NotImplementedError for #auth_headers until a vendor supplies it' do
      expect { bare.send(:auth_headers, 'token') }.to raise_error(NotImplementedError, /auth_headers/)
    end

    it 'raises NotImplementedError for #vendor_error_message until a vendor supplies it' do
      expect { bare.send(:vendor_error_message, {'Error' => 'vendor said no'}) }.to raise_error(NotImplementedError, /vendor_error_message/)
    end

    # Optional, like the transport hook: a vendor that names no decisions in its
    # bodies still gets the status map.
    it 'names no error class of its own until a vendor supplies one' do
      expect(bare.send(:vendor_error_class, {'Error' => 'vendor said no'})).to be_nil
    end

    # The grant's own lifecycle is not a set of hooks: RFC 6749 fixes the grant
    # types, the field names and the challenge method, so the exchange is written
    # once and a vendor owes only the addresses. Every part of it therefore fails
    # the same way — naming the declaration, not the method that needed it.
    it 'tells a vendor that declared no OAuth2 endpoints, asked for a consent url' do
      expect { bare_class.authorization_url(redirect_uri: 'https://app.example/callback', state: 'state', code_challenge: 'challenge') }.to raise_error(NotImplementedError, /\.oauth2_settings/)
    end

    it 'tells a vendor that declared no OAuth2 endpoints, asked to exchange a code' do
      expect { bare.exchange_code!(code: 'ac', redirect_uri: 'https://app.example/callback', code_verifier: 'verifier') }.to raise_error(NotImplementedError, /\.oauth2_settings/)
    end

    it 'tells a vendor that declared no OAuth2 endpoints, asked to withdraw a grant' do
      expect { bare.revoke_tokens! }.to raise_error(NotImplementedError, /\.oauth2_settings/)
    end

    it 'tells a vendor that declared no OAuth2 endpoints, asked to renew a grant' do
      expect { bare.send(:refresh_tokens!) }.to raise_error(NotImplementedError, /\.oauth2_settings/)
    end

  context 'with a successful request' do
    before { stub_vendor_ping(status: 200, body: {'Status' => 'ok'}.to_json) }

    it 'returns the parsed response body' do

    end

        expect(env.request_headers['Authorization']).to eq("Bearer #{connection.access_token}")

module TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::Instead::Mock::Router
  # @param env [Faraday::Env] the outgoing request
  # @param firm_id [Integer] whose handles this response belongs to
  # @return [Array(Integer, Hash, String)] status, headers, serialized body
def call(env, firm_id:)
    route = ROUTES.find { |verb, pattern, _| verb == env.method && pattern.match?(env.url.path) }

    return not_found if route.nil?

    _, pattern, handler = route
    return missing_entity if ENTITY_SCOPED.include?(handler) && env.request_headers[ENTITY_HEADER].blank?

    body = public_send(handler, env, firm_id: firm_id, match: pattern.match(env.url.path))

    [200, JSON_HEADERS, body.to_json]
  end

module TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::Instead::Mock::Router
  # @return [String] an RFC 4122 v5 uuid, which is what the contract declares
def handle(kind, *parts)
    Digest::UUID.uuid_v5(UUID_NAMESPACE, "instead:#{kind}:#{parts.join(':')}")
  end

class TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::BaseClient
  # Order matters: response middleware runs innermost-first, so `:json` has to
  # be registered after the error middleware for the latter to see a parsed body,
  # and the budget is read inside it so a refusal is recorded before it raises.
def apply_error_handling(builder)
    builder.use RaiseCustomErrors, extract_message: method(:vendor_error_message), classify: method(:vendor_error_class)
    builder.use RecordRateLimit, vendor:, api_root_path: URI(base_url).path, rate_limit_group_of: method(:rate_limit_group_of)
    builder.response :json, content_type: /\bjson$/

    builder.adapter(*adapter_spec)
  end

module TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::Instead::Mock::Router
# Reference implementation of a vendor mock transport, wired into nothing:
# no client selects it and no flag reaches it.
#
# The Instead API answered from the request alone.
#
# Every response is a function of what the caller sent. Identifiers are hashed
# from the firm and the input, so the same call yields the same handle and a
# repeated upload is idempotent the way the contract says it is. Nothing is
# stored and nothing advances over time: the vendor exposes no per-document
# state to advance, and a progression with no live counterpart would prove a
# fold that breaks the day the transport is switched.
#
# Where a field cannot be derived from the request it is left out. Every
# property of `File` is optional, so silence is available, and it beats putting
# a fabricated path where a caller reads a real one.
#
# @api private
  JSON_HEADERS = {'Content-Type' => 'application/json'}.freeze

  # Fixed so a handle survives a restart — the ports store these and read them
  # back on a later request.
  UUID_NAMESPACE = Digest::UUID::OID_NAMESPACE

  # The opaque halves of a pre-signed S3 POST. The vendor computes them from its
  # own credentials; nothing on our side reads them, and the byte transfer never
  # leaves this process here.
  UPLOAD_URL = 'https://fs.instead.mock.amazonaws.com/'
  UPLOAD_POLICY = 'bW9jay11cGxvYWQtcG9saWN5'
  UPLOAD_SIGNATURE = '0f3a1c9d2b7e4f6a8c5d1e3b7a9f2c4d6e8b0a1c3d5f7e9b1a3c5d7f9e1b3a5c'
  UPLOAD_TTL_SEC = 900

  ACCESS_TOKEN_TTL_SEC = 3600
  GRANTED_SCOPE = 'entities.list entities.create entities.docs.create entities.docs.read webhooks.entities.docs.upserted webhooks.entities.docs.indexed webhooks.entities.docs.archived'

  # What a listing answers with. Creating an entity does not add to it: a
  # listing that grew would need somewhere to remember, and the ports read the
  # handle off the create response rather than by searching for it. Values are
  # from the contract's `EntityType` enum.
  SEED_ENTITY_TYPES = %w[S_CORP INDIVIDUAL].freeze

  # Verb, path, handler. A request matching nothing here comes back as the
  # vendor's own 404, so a caller reaching for an endpoint the mock does not
  # serve finds out through the client's error tree rather than through a nil.
  ROUTES = [
    [:post, %r{\A/v1/oauth2/token\z}, :token],
    [:post, %r{\A/v1/oauth2/revoke\z}, :revoke],
    [:get, %r{\A/v1/entities\z}, :list_entities],
    [:post, %r{\A/v1/entities\z}, :create_entity],
    [:post, %r{\A/v1/docs/uploads\z}, :start_doc_upload],
    [:put, %r{\A/v1/docs/(?<uuid>[^/]+)\z}, :finalize_doc_upload],
    [:get, %r{\A/v1/docs/(?<uuid>[^/]+)\z}, :get_doc]
  ].freeze

  ENTITY_HEADER = 'X-Instead-Entity-UUID'

  # Document calls act on one entity's files and are refused without the header
  # naming it, as the vendor refuses them.
  ENTITY_SCOPED = %i[start_doc_upload finalize_doc_upload get_doc].freeze

  module_function

  # The contract answers 200 whether or not the token was still live and returns
  # no document, so there is nothing to derive and nothing to report.
  def revoke(_env, **)
    {}
  end

  def timestamp
    Time.current.utc.iso8601
  end

class TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::BaseClient
def http_connection(access_token)
    Faraday.new(url: base_url) do |builder|
      builder.request :json
      builder.headers.update(auth_headers(access_token))
      builder.headers['Accept'] = 'application/json'

      builder.options.timeout = REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SEC
      builder.options.open_timeout = OPEN_TIMEOUT_SEC

      apply_error_handling(builder)
    end
  end

class TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::BaseClient
  # The OAuth2 token endpoint is unauthenticated and form-encoded, so it cannot
  # reuse the JSON connection above — but it shares the error middleware, which
  # is what turns a rejected grant into an {InvalidGrantError}. Its own timeout
  # applies here: this is the call made under the connection row lock.
  #
  # @return [Faraday::Connection] for a vendor's `refresh_tokens!` to post to
def token_connection
    Faraday.new(url: base_url) do |builder|
      builder.request :url_encoded

      builder.options.timeout = TOKEN_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SEC
      builder.options.open_timeout = OPEN_TIMEOUT_SEC

      apply_error_handling(builder)
    end
  end

class TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::BaseClient
  # A pre-signed target is a URL of its own — a bucket, not the vendor — so this
  # connection is built with no root to resolve against and carries no
  # authorization headers. It shares the error middleware all the same: a
  # refusal from the bucket has to reach a caller as the same typed error a
  # refusal from the vendor does.
  #
  # @return [Faraday::Connection] for {#upload_to_signed_target} to post to
def upload_connection
    Faraday.new do |builder|
      builder.request :multipart

      builder.options.timeout = UPLOAD_TIMEOUT_SEC
      builder.options.open_timeout = OPEN_TIMEOUT_SEC

      apply_error_handling(builder)
    end
  end

module TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::Instead::Mock::Router
  # Both halves rotate, and they rotate off whatever was presented — the refresh
  # token on a renewal, the authorization code on the first exchange. The next
  # renewal carries a different refresh token and therefore derives a different
  # pair; one that returned the token it just replaced would leave the
  # forced-refresh path unable to tell it succeeded.
def token(env, firm_id:, **)
    form = Rack::Utils.parse_nested_query(env.body.to_s)
    presented = form['refresh_token'] || form['code']

    {
      access_token: opaque_token('ia_at', firm_id, presented),
      token_type: 'Bearer',
      expires_in: ACCESS_TOKEN_TTL_SEC,
      refresh_token: opaque_token('ia_rt', firm_id, presented),
      scope: GRANTED_SCOPE,
      firm_uuid: handle('firm', firm_id)
    }
  end

module TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::Instead::Mock::Router
  # The vendor holds files per entity, so the handle is minted from the entity the
  # call names as well as the path within it.
def start_doc_upload(env, firm_id:, **)
    attributes = parsed_body(env)
    uuid = handle('file', firm_id, env.request_headers[ENTITY_HEADER], attributes['Path'])

    {FileUUID: uuid, Upload: signed_upload(uuid, attributes['Path'])}
  end

class TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::BaseClient
  # Refusals a status cannot tell apart, named by the vendor in the body through
  # {#vendor_error_class}. Each carries a decision the caller makes differently
  # from the status it arrived with, and stays a kind of that status's class so a
  # caller rescuing the status is not broken by a vendor learning to name it.
  # Only the refusals every vendor can make live here; one spoken by a single
  # vendor belongs on that vendor's client.
  #
  # The firm is over its plan with the vendor — waiting does not help.
  class QuotaExceededError < RequestError; end

  # Retried as a group: both mean "this attempt could not present a usable
  # token". The lock timeout belongs here because the refresh sets one, so a
  # request racing another worker's renewal fails on the lock, not on the vendor.
  AUTH_ERRORS = [UnauthorizedError, ActiveRecord::LockWaitTimeout].freeze

  # Status => [error class, i18n key used when the vendor sends no message].
  # Adding a vendor means filling the hooks below, never touching this table.
  ERRORS_MAP = {
    400 => [BadRequestError, 'bad_request'],
    401 => [UnauthorizedError, 'unauthorized'],
    403 => [ForbiddenError, 'forbidden'],
    404 => [NotFoundError, 'not_found'],
    422 => [UnprocessableEntityError, 'unprocessable_entity'],
    423 => [LockedError, 'locked'],
    429 => [RateLimitedError, 'rate_limited'],
    500 => [ServerError, 'server_error'],
    503 => [ServiceUnavailableError, 'service_unavailable']
  }.freeze

  private

  attr_reader :vendor_connection, :transport

  # Optional: a vendor that names a decision in its failure body — a quota, a
  # missing scope — maps it onto one of the classes that carry one. Answering
  # `nil` leaves the status to decide.
  #
  # @param body [Hash, String, nil] parsed response body
  # @return [Class, nil] a {RequestError} subclass
  def vendor_error_class(_body)
    nil
  end

  # Vendor hooks. `refresh_tokens!` is the fourth, and belongs to
  # {TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::TokenRefreshable}.

class TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::BaseClient
  class RaiseCustomErrors < Faraday::Middleware
def on_complete(env)
      status = env.response.status
      return if status < 400

      status_class, i18n_key = ERRORS_MAP.fetch(status) { fallback_for(status) }

      body = env.response.body
      error_class = @classify.call(body) || status_class
      message = @extract_message.call(body).presence || I18n.t(i18n_key, scope: I18N_ERRORS_SCOPE)

      raise error_class.new(message, body:, code: status, headers: env.response.headers)
    end

class TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::BaseClient
  class RaiseCustomErrors < Faraday::Middleware
    # What an unnamed failure becomes. The map earns a caller the right to tell
    # one failure from another; a status missing from it is still a failure, and
    # saying nothing would return the raw body where a parsed one is expected — a
    # gateway's HTML 502 then reads as "the vendor has nothing for you".
def fallback_for(status)
      return [ServerError, 'server_error'] if status >= 500

      [RequestError, 'unexpected_error']
    end

class TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::BaseClient
  # `measure` returns the elapsed time, not the block's value — capture it.
  #
  # @param operation [String] one of the `operation` tag's values, declared with
  #   the metric group in `config/initializers/yabeda.rb`
def measured(operation)
    result = nil
    Yabeda.tax_automations.requests_duration.measure(vendor:, operation:) { result = yield }

    result
  end

class TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::BaseClient
def track_failure(operation, reason)
    Yabeda.tax_automations.failed_requests_total.increment({vendor:, operation:, reason:})
  end

module TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::TokenRefreshable
  # The token endpoint's own failures. Nothing above this layer sees these three
  # calls, so a refusal counted nowhere else is counted here.
  #
  # Named in full for the reason {#refresh!} gives below: the error classes belong
  # to the one class this module is mixed into.
def measured_token_call(operation, &)
    measured(operation, &)
  rescue TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::BaseClient::RequestError => e
    track_failure(operation, "HTTP_ERROR: #{e.code}")
    raise
  rescue *TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::BaseClient::NETWORK_ERRORS => e
    track_failure(operation, "NETWORK_ERROR: #{e.class.name}")
    raise
  end

module TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::TokenRefreshable
  # Which ceremony the exchange belongs to, in the words of the `operation` tag.
  # Read before the grant is stored — after it, every row says the same thing.
def exchange_operation
    vendor_connection.connected_at.present? ? 'reconnect' : 'connect'
  end

module TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::TokenRefreshable
  # Withdraws the grant on the vendor's side. Only the refresh token is named: it
  # is what a renewal would present, and the access token dies with the grant.
  #
  # The app names itself here as it does on the exchange. A vendor that checks
  # refuses an unnamed caller, and the refusal would go unread: the port
  # disconnects the firm whatever the vendor answered, so the row would say the
  # grant is gone while it is still live.
  #
  # Moving the row is the service layer's job — this reaches the vendor and
  # returns.

  AUTH_RETRY_TIMEOUT_SEC = 2

  OPEN_TIMEOUT_SEC = 5
  # Ordinary calls carry small JSON documents — file bytes go straight to the
  # vendor's pre-signed target and never pass through here.
  REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SEC = 30

  # Faraday spends this on each read from and write to the socket rather than on
  # the transfer as a whole, so it is a threshold for a stalled connection, not a
  # budget for the bytes: a slow upload that keeps moving is never cut short by
  # it. The value is the one the AWS SDK carries for the same kind of timeout
  # against the same kind of endpoint — a bucket that has said nothing for a
  # minute has stopped listening.
  UPLOAD_TIMEOUT_SEC = 60

  # locked, so it answers to that lock rather than to the budget above: it has
  # to finish before a worker waiting on the same row gives up. Faraday counts
  # its two phases in sequence — `open_timeout` establishes the connection, and
  # only then does the `timeout` clock start — so both are subtracted.

  #   pre-signed target is several of its fields at once, and reading them is the
  #   vendor's vocabulary rather than the transport's

  #   whole response when one is given

        # The renewal rides an operation of its own: its wait on the row lock says
        # nothing about how fast the vendor's API is.

      # metric that only sees the last one hides the ladder.

      # next attempt has to carry one it minted rather than the one it just
      # rejected.

    # must not fall through to the counting branch below. A lock timeout is not
    # an authorization failure at all and has nothing of the vendor to carry.

    # act on. Counted here because it reaches the caller through none of the
    # branches around it — the token module raises it in place of whatever the
    # vendor said.

module TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::TokenRefreshable
  # Turns the code a completed ceremony carried back into the grant. Public,
  # unlike the renewal: the service layer drives it, because a grant that does not
  # exist yet cannot be renewed on demand. Unauthenticated, so it needs no live
  # connection — only the row naming the firm, which decides the transport.
  #
  # A refusal leaves as the status the vendor sent rather than as
  # {InvalidGrantError}: there is no grant yet for a refusal to be about.
  #
  # @param code [String]
  # @param redirect_uri [String] the one the authorize request declared
  # @param code_verifier [String] the PKCE verifier behind the challenge
  # @return [Hash] `{access_token:, refresh_token:, expires_in:, refresh_expires_in:}`
  #   plus whatever {#grant_identity} reads off the same response
def exchange_code!(code:, redirect_uri:, code_verifier:)
    body = token_response(exchange_operation, grant_type: 'authorization_code', code:, redirect_uri:, code_verifier:)

    tokens_from(body).merge(grant_identity(body))
  end

module TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::TokenRefreshable
  # Renews under the row lock. The re-check inside the lock is what makes a
  # concurrent caller a waiter rather than a second refresher.
  #
  # @param force [Boolean] the vendor rejected the token we hold, so its stored
  #   expiry says nothing — renewing is right unless another caller has already
  #   replaced that very token.
def refresh!(force: false)
    reject_grant!(I18n.t('invalid_grant', scope: I18N_ERRORS_SCOPE)) unless vendor_connection.refresh_token_valid?

    rejected_token = vendor_connection.access_token if force

    # On its own DB connection, so the write outlives a rollback of the caller's
    # transaction. The vendor has already rotated the refresh token by then, and
    # a rolled-back row keeps a token the vendor no longer honours — the grant is
    # dead with no way back.
    ThreadHelper.run_in_new_thread do
      Thread.current.report_on_exception = false

      vendor_connection.transaction(requires_new: true) do
        # Bounds the wait when the caller's own transaction already holds this
        # row: what would be a deadlock against the thread above surfaces as a
        # LockWaitTimeout the client retries.
        ActiveRecord::Base.connection.execute("SET LOCAL lock_timeout = '#{CONNECTION_LOCK_TIMEOUT_SEC}s'")

        vendor_connection.with_lock do
          # The guard at the door read the row as it stood when the request began;
          # this reads it as it stands now. A withdrawal that landed while we
          # queued behind the lock leaves a row the transition below does not lead
          # out of, and the caller is owed the same error as any other dead grant.
          raise InvalidGrantError.new(I18n.t('invalid_grant', scope: I18N_ERRORS_SCOPE), connection: vendor_connection) unless vendor_connection.may_refresh?

          # Whoever held the lock before us may have renewed already, and what
          # counts as "already" depends on what sent us here: preemptively any
          # unexpired token will do, but after a rejection only one that is no
          # longer the token the vendor turned down.
          next if force && vendor_connection.access_token != rejected_token
          next if !force && vendor_connection.access_token_valid?

          vendor_connection.store_tokens!(**refresh_tokens!)
          # The exchange settles the grant's standing in both directions, so the
          # transition follows it either way: here it stamps `refreshed_at` and
          # brings an expired grant back to connected, and in {#reject_grant!} it
          # moves a refused one further out.
          vendor_connection.refresh!
        end
      end
    end
    # Named in full because the exchange reaches the token endpoint through the
    # including client's error middleware — the one place this module knows it is
    # mixed into exactly one class.
  rescue TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::BaseClient::RequestError => e
    raise unless grant_refused?(e)

    reject_grant!(e.message)
  end

module TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::TokenRefreshable
  # Presents the refresh token for a new pair. Persisting is {#refresh!}'s job.
  #
  # @return [Hash] `{access_token:, refresh_token:, expires_in:, refresh_expires_in:}`

    tokens_from(token_response('token_refresh', grant_type: 'refresh_token', refresh_token: vendor_connection.refresh_token))
  end

  # names — so one request serves the first exchange and every renewal after it.

  # over {TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::BaseClient#token_connection} rather than
  # the JSON one.

    self.class.declared_oauth2!

    measured_token_call(operation) { token_connection.post(relative_path(oauth2_paths[:token]), grant.merge(client_credentials)) }.body
  end

module Crm
  module Api
    module Contact
      # The contact a portal user acts as on an account: the account's non-deleted
      # contact whose emails hold the user's email, lowest id first. Returns the
      # `find` row under `contact`, or `contact: nil` when the user is not linked
      # to the account or has no such contact. The caller renders shortcodes
      # from the row itself; CRM only resolves the user → contact rule.
      #
      # @param account_id [Integer]
      # @param user_id [Integer] portal user whose contact is looked up
      # @return [Result] success: { contact: { contact_id, contact_name, first_name,
      #   middle_name, last_name, email, phone, account_id, country, company_name,
      #   street_address, city, province, zip, custom_fields: [{id, name, kind,
      #   shortcode_value}], account_full_name } | nil }; reason: :not_authorized
      #   on cross-firm/non-existent account or policy denial (`:not_found`
      #   collapses to `:not_authorized`). `ArgumentError` on `actor.firm_id != firm.id`.
def find_by_account_user(firm:, user:, actor:, account_id:, user_id:)
        raise ArgumentError, "actor.firm_id (#{actor.firm_id}) does not match firm.id (#{firm.id})" if actor.firm_id != firm.id

        result = Crm::Contacts::FindByAccountUser.call(user, actor, firm, account_id, user_id)

        if result.successful?
          {success: true, errors: {}, data: {contact: result.data && contact_data(result.data)}}
        else
          {success: false, errors: result.errors, reason: FIND_BY_ACCOUNT_USER_REASON_MAP.fetch(result.reason), data: nil}
        end
      rescue AbstractPolicy::PolicyError => e
        {success: false, errors: {base: [e.message]}, reason: :not_authorized, data: nil}
      end
